label: D1 after unrewarded S1 visit, ramping up over episode trials 70-99
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") * np.clip(ep_trial - 70, 0, 30) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") * (ep_trial >= 90) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * np.clip(ep_trial - 70, 0, 30) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (ep_trial >= 90) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == -1) * (in_rew == 0) * np.clip(ep_trial - 70, 0, 30)
explanation: Sparse feature (nonzero on 1.1% of steps), active only at D1. Its magnitude is set by the previous trial having reached S1 and gone unrewarded, gated by how late the episode is: near zero before trial ~70, then rising roughly linearly, with a step up at trial >= 90. After a1 S1 u (common) it is strongest (fitted about 1.1 at trials 90+), about twice the value after a2 S1 u (rare, about 0.5). Unrewarded S2 visits and rewarded trials of any kind leave it at about 0. On a window first trial, where the previous trial is unknown, an unrewarded D1 late in the episode gives a small extra contribution. All terms are observed. Timing alone gives R^2 0.12. These 5 terms give R^2 beyond timing of 0.71 on dev and 0.70 on test. That is far above the profile additive ceiling (all = 0.13), because the effect is an interaction between last trial and episode time. Value, policy, the hidden good state and future variables were not needed.

issues: The 'ramps roughly linearly from trial 70' wording is too smooth. Splitting by decile on test gives a1 S1 u weights of 0.08 / 0.45 / 1.12 for deciles 7 / 8 / 9 and a2 S1 u weights of ~0 / ~0 / 0.48. So after a2 S1 u there is no ramp at all (clip weight 0.003), only a step at trial 90, and a1 S1 u is mostly a step at decile 9 with a small rise in decile 8. The decile model scores 0.674 on test.

The first-window-trial term (prev unknown, in_rew==0) has a small weight because the previous trial is unknown, not because the activation there is small. The worst misses are all first-trial cells with actual ~1.2-1.6 against predicted ~0.3. Per-decile indicators (0.014 / 0.066 / 0.177) add nothing (test 0.6957). These errors are not observable from the available variables, so this is an irreducible gap rather than a label error.

The claim that value was not needed is not quite right. Within late a1 S1 u and a2 S1 u, a lower model value raises the activation: weights of -0.23 and -0.35 per unit value at trials 90+. Adding these terms raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.695 to 0.766-0.769. This is a moderate effect, not a large systematic gap.

The remaining checks hold. Misses on the original terms show no systematic phase or previous-trial error class: GO and D2 are off by +0.005 and D1 by -0.010, and no D1 previous-trial pattern is over-predicted by more than 0.015. Only D1 activity, a1 S1 u being about 2x a2 S1 u at trials 90+ (about 1.1 vs about 0.5 fitted), near zero after S2-unrewarded or rewarded trials, and no future variables all check out. Test 0.695 is confirmed.
Trial-before history (two consecutive unrewarded S1 visits, the earlier choice), the hidden good state and the policy logit add nothing: test 0.695, 0.694 and 0.701.
